dek: Since I was a kid, I've wanted to rebuild the fishing game from Breath of Fire III as a mobile app, and expand on an experience I was so attached to. The game came out on PlayStation in 1997. I decrypted the program on a disc I own, decompiled all of it, and rebuilt Fishing Mode in TypeScript and Phaser 4 rather than emulating it. The rebuild runs in a browser at the game's native 480×272, and once it matched the original I built on top of it: save files, four playable fishers, a shop, a jukebox and support for any screen and any controller.
short: Breath of Fire III's fishing mode, decrypted from a disc I own, decompiled with Ghidra (11,676 functions) and rebuilt in TypeScript and Phaser 4 rather than emulated, then extended with save files, four fishers and a 128-track jukebox.

delivery.summary: From an encrypted disc image to a playable, extended browser port. The repository holds no game data: the extractors read it from the owner's own disc.

steps.name: Decrypt
steps.detail: pspdecrypt turns the encrypted EBOOT.BIN into a relocatable MIPS (Allegrex) program.

steps.name: Decompile
steps.detail: Ghidra 12.2 headless with ghidra-allegrex and a custom export script writes every function out as C.

steps.name: Trace
steps.detail: The fish table, matched against a PS1 speedrun's star table, located the fishing logic. Fishing turned out to run on world-map areas.

steps.name: Extract
steps.detail: Node tools decode tiled textures, per-strip palettes, terrain meshes, sound banks and music: about 830 files.

steps.name: Rebuild
steps.detail: Phaser 4 and TypeScript, with a PSX-style affine triangle renderer for the terrain. Every layout measured against reference screenshots.

steps.name: Extend
steps.detail: Three save files, four fishers, a shop, a gallery, a jukebox, cheats, a CRT mode, 1–4× scaling and any input.

highlights.title: Rebuilt, not emulated
highlights.text: No emulator runs the original code. The port re-implements the fishing rules, casting, the lure rhythm and the fights in TypeScript, read from the decompiled program.

highlights.title: Measured against the original
highlights.text: Six screenshots from the real hardware set every layout, so sprite positions and window sizes were measured rather than guessed.

highlights.title: Past the original
highlights.text: Three save files, Young Ryu, Ryu, Young Nina and Nina as playable fishers, the Manillo shop, a gallery, a 128-track music player, cheats, a CRT TV mode and any screen at 1–4× or fill.

highlights.title: Any input
highlights.text: Keyboard, mouse, game controllers, touch and an on-screen pad, with a controls screen in PlayStation symbols.

highlights.title: Tooling for the next one
highlights.text: An animation viewer and sheet editor, URL flags for testing, and a porting playbook written up so the method carries to other games.
